To this end, we propose the Pose-Transformed Image (PTI) framework, which uses pose information to create virtual background images and improved depth cues for object recognition. We also introduce the Pose-Transformed Image Dataset (PVT) for training single-view 3D object pose estimation models. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach and highlight its potential as a game-changing training paradigm for 3D object pose estimation.

In semiconductor-superconductor heterostructures, non-standard hybrid states can form, even in the absence of direct coupling between the layers. These states can still induce significant interactions between Majorana modes located on different ends of a chain. In a setup consisting of two chains with Andreev states from a Y-junction or a chain with Andreev states from two distinct junctions, the interactions between the states can create a tunneling effect or facilitate indirect interactions between Majorana modes. The resulting interactions are typically strong enough to drive the formation of topological modes, even without local interactions between the layers.

Magnetic reconnection is a widespread phenomenon in various astrophysical environments, accelerating particles in the process. However, the underlying mechanism of magnetic reconnection in a one-dimensional current sheet is still not fully understood. A new study on 3D magnetic reconnection in a planet's magnetosphere offers new insights into particle acceleration dynamics. The research reveals that the acceleration of particles is not only dependent on local electric fields, but also heavily influenced by the diffusion of particles along the magnetic field and across the current sheet. Furthermore, the study finds that the diffusion of particles across the current sheet plays a crucial role in transporting energy to the outer regions of the current sheet, contributing to the acceleration of magnetic reconnection. The findings suggest that the diffusion of particles is a critical component of magnetic reconnection in 3D current sheets.

We calculate one-loop corrections to the Higgsstrahlung process in extended scalar sector models, specifically the CP-even 3HDM, demonstrating that these corrections can be substantial. Considering a Higgsstrahlung process involving a top quark decay, we observe a significant amplification of the one-loop correction, with this effect potentially influencing the overall cross-section. Notably, our results exhibit sensitivity to the chosen model, underpinning the necessity of comprehensive numerical evaluations for models beyond the Standard Model.
A formula for the subdifferential of the joint numerical radius is developed and utilized to investigate the best approximation problem associated with this quantity.

As more industries transition to AI, there's a corresponding increase in the amount of financial data being processed, which poses a significant risk of exposure. This is particularly concerning for data-intensive sectors like financial markets, where a data breach can have severe consequences for businesses and individuals. This vulnerability creates an opportunity for attackers to exploit, which is why it's essential to protect financial data in institutions through robust security measures. This research assesses the effectiveness of AI-based frameworks in safeguarding financial data and compares them to conventional methods. We evaluated the performance of AI-based frameworks on simulated trading patterns, finding that they were notably more successful. This outcome underscores the need to adopt secure data protection practices in financial institutions and supports the implementation of AI-based frameworks as a viable solution.

This research paper explores the link between multivariate stochastic mappings and linear operators on Hilbert spaces by using an approach based on kernel analysis. Our primary goal is to establish a framework that enables the identification of kernels associated with second-order stochastic mappings, thus providing a solution to a problem that has been unresolved since 2006. By drawing on existing results in multivariate stochastic mappings and Hilbert space operators, we develop a theory of kernels for these mappings, allowing us to build on the established foundation of kernel theory in probability and statistics. By employing this framework, we are able to define a multivariate process as a kernel-based operator applied to a linear operator, thus connecting various areas of study in the field.

Researchers investigating the ignition of high-pressure hydrogen-oxygen mixtures, specifically those containing hydrogen and oxygen at pressures exceeding 100 bar, have encountered difficulties in identifying the precise ignition mechanism. A recent study employed a detailed kinetic model to analyze the ignition process and thermal stability of hydrogen-oxygen mixtures, utilizing a large-scale reaction mechanism with over 52,000 unique reactions. The study revealed that, within a specific pressure range, the ignition process is triggered by a three-step combustion mechanism. The mechanism's rate constants were determined by fitting the model to experimental data obtained from high-pressure combustion experiments, specifically those conducted by Wang et al. in 2011. The study also showed that, at pressures above 200 bar, the ignition process is triggered by a combustion wave. The study's results, specifically its temperature-dependent ignition delay times, were validated against experimental data obtained from two separate high-pressure combustion setups, a rapid compression machine and a shock tube, yielding a relatively small deviation of less than 30%.

We introduce a Boundary-Aware Segmentation Network (BASNet) that leverages
attention to focus on object boundaries, refining both saliency prediction and
post-processing for enhanced segmentation accuracy. Building on the attention
module's ability to target specific features, our approach incorporates
multi-scale boundary detection and edge attention enhancement to improve its
performance. In the post-processing stage, a boundary-guided voting mechanism
estimates missing object boundaries, while an object- and boundary-embedding
loss function is introduced to fine-tune the model. We evaluate BASNet on
various datasets, achieving state-of-the-art results on ACDC, CardiDW, and
FundusDB, as well as competitive performance on Montico, and outperforming
existing state-of-the-art boundary-aware methods.

Connected autonomous vehicles (CAVs) rely on data from sensors and V2X messages to enhance situational awareness, but the effectiveness of this information is crucial and time-sensitive. Therefore, it's essential to prioritize and process critical data in a timely manner. However, current V2X protocols lack built-in capabilities to manage situational awareness, making it necessary for CAVs to develop their own communication strategies. This paper presents a study on developing an advanced, prioritized CAV control system, known as V2X-PCA, that leverages both local and remote data to make informed decisions. V2X-PCA utilizes machine learning and deep reinforcement learning to optimize system performance, and its efficacy is evaluated using simulated traffic scenarios under varying conditions.

We examine the behavior of active Brownian particles that interact with a wall, taking into account the possibility of them sticking together in a localized area when they collide. This phenomenon leads to the formation of temporary clusters that move across the surface, and as a result, the particles within the cluster experience higher fluid densities and stronger interactions with their surroundings compared to isolated particles. These characteristics result in the emergence of a specific type of boundary layer that influences the flow of fluid near the boundary, and we demonstrate that this effect intensifies with the activity level of the particles. To better understand this phenomenon, we study a simplified model of 'active sticky particles' and use it to gain insight into the more complex scenario of active Brownian particles with short-range interactions.

A novel method has been devised for solving the radial portion of the time-dependent two-component non-equilibrium Lindhart equation. This involves dividing the time-dependent wave function into Siegert states, a unique formulation of atomic states adapted to non-stationary conditions. Each Siegert state is characterized by an energy parameter and associated radial wave functions, much like traditional atomic models. However, these new states incorporate velocity-dependent mass corrections and account for interactions with real photons. This approach yields a time-dependent wave function, enabling the calculation and visualization of dynamic cross-sections for photoionization processes. Notably, the method can be extended to include additional physical factors such as collisions, electron scattering, and x-ray interactions.

A newly discovered ultrafast wave in the solar corona is a brief, rapidly moving disturbance in the Sun's plasma, which was first observed using high-resolution imaging. This phenomenon, which was found in various solar flares, is characterized by sudden changes in the intensity and velocity of certain solar rays. Analysis suggests that these disturbances are caused by the rapid movement of solar plasma along tangled magnetic lines, with the frequency and speed of this movement linked to the intensity and velocity of specific solar rays. Observations also indicate that a certain type of solar ray is more intense during this phenomenon, which is likely caused by the rapid movement of solar plasma between the disturbance and a solar surface. This phenomenon, which is called a moving emission patch, is a temporary and dynamic disturbance in the Sun's plasma, as opposed to a stationary one observed in the past.

In this work, we investigate how a certain term affects the way color fields behave in quantum chromodynamics, specifically when they are confined in a space that is curved and bounded. The research shows that a topological theta term, when considering its effects up to a certain point, causes the fields to collapse more quickly within this curved space. This leads to an interesting interaction between the fields and the boundary of this space, where a solution is found that meets the conditions at the boundary, as long as the curvature remains positive.

Theoretical models for ion-beam mixing in multi-layered systems, particularly those utilizing amorphous implants, have been developed and applied to a specific two-layer structure. It is found that the system's response to ion irradiation can be described by a critical angle, dependent on the system's boundaries and the conditions of implantation. The properties of this critical angle were investigated in relation to ion species, implantation energy, and the interface between layers. It was discovered that the system's composition and the ion's range are key factors influencing this critical angle. Furthermore, the concept of a virtual virtual interface was introduced, representing a boundary beneath which the implantation's effects are largely diminished. It was observed that the implantation energy significantly affects this virtual interface, and the implantation dose influences the mixing rate beyond this interface.

This paper introduces an innovative source code anti-plagiarism method, which utilizes cryptographic techniques - hash functions and symmetric key encryption, to ensure the reliability of source code by safeguarding against modifications. The proposed method, specifically designed for operating systems, incorporates hash functions to generate unique code object codes for each program and secure them with symmetric encryption, making it impossible for third-party plugins to tamper with the code without detection. To verify the effectiveness of this approach, we have implemented a proof-of-concept using Java and assessed its practicality. The method employs code object codes, generated through hash functions, to facilitate efficient reuse detection and improve overall system performance. The integration of hash functions enables the detection of exact matches in reused code objects, while a symmetric key-encrypted source code ensures protection against unauthorized modifications. The proposed method provides a novel solution to traditional source code anti-plagiarism challenges by shielding the code from malicious third-party plugins and maintaining its integrity. The solution offers a practical approach to ensure the security and reliability of source code in software development and development environments.

We consider the Dirichlet series F(s) of the form $F(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{a_n}{n^s}$ with a degree less than d, implying that only the initial d terms are non-zero in the numerator. We connect this to a degree d+1 form $G(s)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{b_n}{n^s}$ where the coefficients $b_n$ arise from the coefficients $a_n$ through a rational transformation, allowing for a degree d+1 form with potentially many more non-zero coefficients. We then investigate the joint growth of F(s) and G(s) over various complex numbers, proving that if G(s) converges absolutely for sufficiently large real parts of s, then F(s) and G(s) share a common region of convergence.

We define a $(k,r)$-metric approximate subgroup $A$ in a group $G$ as a subset with properties: for any two elements $g_1, g_2 \in A$, their product $g_1g_2$ either lies in $A$ with an exponent close to $k$ or is at a distance $r$ from $A$ through element-wise multiplication. A $(k,r)$-metric approximate subgroup with $r<1/n$ has size $n^k$. We identify subgroups in metric approximate subgroups and establish that their centralizer is also a metric approximate subgroup. We establish a connection between metric approximate subgroups and expanders by proving that a metric approximate subgroup with certain conditions is expanders. We apply these findings to show the size of sets generated by products of elements in subgroups.

In nonparametric statistics, estimating log-concave densities is a highly sought-after problem, and a key challenge is developing efficient methods for doing so, as many existing approaches are computationally costly or prone to failure. This work introduces a new, robust, and efficient algorithm, ISLOCO, for estimating log-concave densities, and it achieves this goal by leveraging Ising approximation. By utilizing a sophisticated optimization technique, ISLOCO can handle a wide range of maximum likelihood estimates without issues. Furthermore, our method excels in terms of computational efficiency, as its running time is remarkably fast, often on par with existing approaches, and it demonstrates superior robustness against local maxima. We also propose an extension to our algorithm that enables density-based inference for a range of statistical tests, including the Wald test, and it performs well even in complex scenarios.

We apply the Wang-Landau algorithm to a Monte Carlo sampling strategy for granular systems, enabling us to explore a wide range of static configurations and efficiently compute their statistical properties. We validate the accuracy of this approach by analyzing static friction in bimodal friction-based frictional contact models and discrete frictionless particles with localized defects that experience plastic flow under loading conditions, all while considering size and size-power laws for various granular media.

The game introduced by Ietzi Oshman is a two-player game called Explorer-Director. In this game, Explorer tries to find every $x$-coordinate of a certain subset of $\mathbb{Z}^2$, explained by a "story", while Director helps by suggesting a point each turn. The Explorer's goal is to find the desired points with the fewest number of turns, and they are given a bound on the number of points to find, denoted by $N$. We present improved bounds on the number of turns required, superseding earlier results and extending the $N=100$ case to larger $N$.

The paper introduces a novel method for estimating parameters in stochastic processes. This approach leverages the lower-triangular Cholesky decomposition to transform covariance matrices into parameter values. Leverage is made of the known variance of stochastic processes like Brownian motion, the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, and their specific parameters. Variance and frequency-frequency correlation of these processes are calculated through Cholesky decompositions, allowing for the quantification of parameters like diffusion, drift, and the memory time constant. This method is tested using Brownian motion, the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, and processes combining Brownian motion and diffusion. Results show the proposed method can accurately estimate parameters from a single realization, outperforming the Fourier spectral method in cases of non-stationary processes.

In this paper, the one-dimensional higher-order Broer-Kaup system is analyzed through a consistent tanh expansion, confirming its solvability using this method. Exact interactions between diverse nonlinear phenomena, such as solitons, rational and periodic waves, with initial conditions including breathers, Kruzhkov ones, and N-soliton solutions, are successfully derived. The corresponding profiles for these interactions are visually represented.

The conservation of energy in the incompressible 2D Euler equations is demonstrated to be preserved when vorticity is controlled, with upper bounds on vorticity and velocity established to ensure this conservation. These results are achieved through the design of a dissipative filter which locally removes vorticity and velocity while being compact and localized both in space and time. This method is applicable to the Navier-Stokes equations as well, enabling the proof of a logarithmic decay of energy in both space and time without the need for smallness or regularity assumptions.

VIRUP is a C++ open-source tool that enables users to explore large-scale, 3D visual data by mapping visual features to 3D geometry and utilizing pose information from a head tracking system to create an immersive, motion-linked experience. Although initially designed for visualizing large-scale point clouds, the tool has also been successfully applied to display video data, tracked objects, and virtual reality applications with virtual levels and interactive elements. With its highly responsive 60fps rendering and seamless 3D navigation, users can effortlessly explore vast datasets spanning billions of points. 

The VIRUP software is now publicly available under the GNU General Public License on GitHub, offering a user-friendly, open-source solution for large-scale data exploration. The tool's comprehensive documentation and online tutorials, combined with its collaborative community, aim to empower users to create custom projects and share their knowledge with others.

The Data Bricks Space Mission is a hands-on learning activity grounded in data
physicalization, developed to help kids aged 10-12 understand data principles.
Drawing on research and input from elementary educators, the initiative utilizes
a narrative-driven space exploration with Lego bricks, enabling teachers to help
kids collect, analyze, and present data in an engaging way, promoting data literacy.

In a software-defined networking (SDN) setup, network traffic is routed through specific sequences of network devices, known as data-paths, determined by network control plane instructions. However, the actual data-paths in a network can deviate from the intended ones due to network users' actions, as SDN relies on user trust that control commands will be executed as intended. To ensure data-paths conform to predefined policies, network control in SDN relies on network management requiring network data-paths in real-time. To determine whether a network is functioning according to its intended data-paths, researchers identified two critical criteria: first, the network should be in a state where its control commands can be executed without obstacles; second, all control commands should be in line with the intended data-paths. To determine whether these criteria are met, researchers developed a method to verify if there are any operational data-paths in a network by examining if it's possible to simulate the network's control commands in a network environment where its control commands are in line with its intended data-paths. To simulate a network's control commands in a real-time environment, researchers identified a method to transform SDN control commands into a sequence of network operations, and to verify that a network's control commands can be executed, researchers developed a method to verify that a network's control commands can be executed, by simulating its control commands and checking for any inconsistencies. To implement these findings, researchers developed a tool called V-Veri

Enforcing disentanglement in neural representations is complicated due to factors such as overlapping features and interdependent dimensions. To improve disentanglement performance, research has shown that improving feature quality improves the disentanglement outcome, as seen in the increased effectiveness of disentanglement in transformation-invariant representations. We verify this relationship by testing the influence of feature quality on disentanglement in a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) using the synthetic dataset. We also demonstrate how the type of feature used affects the disentanglement performance of the encoder.

The energy-harvesting efficiency from water flow for a specific type of foil configuration has been investigated. This configuration involves two foils placed in close proximity, with a focus on how their distance apart affects power generation. To analyze this, a computational model was used to simulate the flow of water around the foils and calculate the energy transferred. This was done for various distances and flow speeds, with the results showing a specific optimal distance where the energy generation was highest. This optimal distance was found to be dependent on the flow speed, allowing for a way to maximize power output through adjusting the foil spacing. This optimal distance was found to be around 1.5 times the foil's length for high flow speeds and as low as 0.5 times for low flow speeds. This optimal distance was found to be around 1.5 times the foil's length for high flow speeds and as low as 0.5 times for low flow speeds.

Extracting spectral functions from lattice QCD data with high precision is difficult due to the complex and non-linear nature of the functional fit and the limited sampling of the QCD parameter space. Bayesian inference can be a powerful tool in this context, but its effectiveness is uncertain due to the large dimensionality of the free energy functional. To address this issue, we propose a new Bayesian approach that combines spectral reconstruction with domain expert knowledge. By incorporating physical constraints, we can transform the high-dimensional posterior into a tractable problem. We also introduce a new Bayesian inference algorithm that employs these physical constraints to fine-tune the fitting process. By incorporating constraints related to the low-lying states of the excited charmonia, we can significantly improve the accuracy and stability of the fitting process.

We have successfully observed the charge-tunneling phenomenon occurring between a quantum dot and a superconducting island using a technique called radio-frequency spectroscopy in a system at low temperatures. By analyzing the results, we were able to identify the emergence of Andreev tunneling in the Coulomb diamond structure, characteristic of a system where charge tunneling is superconducting. The data also shows that our device is capable of detecting very small energy levels, with values as low as 0.4 micro-electron volts. Furthermore, we observed an unusual asymmetry in the detection of tunneling patterns when the superconducting island and quantum dot energies are reversed, indicating a clear distinction between the two in terms of energy levels.

The central objective in the field of drug discovery is to identify key biological targets involved in disease progression. Advances in data availability, computational power, and the development of predictive models have shifted the focus of drug target identification from experimental approaches towards in silico methods. This study leverages graph-based analysis and machine learning techniques, utilizing a comprehensive network of human proteins, to classify potential disease-causing targets. By employing a two-stage approach combining machine learning classifiers and a graph-based ranking algorithm, this research aims to enhance the precision and recall of target identification. Results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach in pinpointing known disease-associated targets, with the ranking algorithm providing a complementary method for generating candidate protein interaction partners.

This informal document assesses various implementations of lambda-calculus, 
focusing on their core components and compilation strategies. It's crucial to 
note that the evaluations that follow are not comprehensive analyses but 
instead provide a snapshot of key considerations. While not intended as a 
comprehensive benchmark, this document doesn't address all relevant aspects 
of implementations either. Please see the GitHub repository for a more in-depth 
analysis, additional comparisons, and a detailed evaluation of the underlying 
microbenchmarks.

The Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) and the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) form a significant interaction zone within the South Pole Wall, a vast structure, located within the Vicinity of the Milky Way galaxy.  The study of the LMC and SMC interaction has provided valuable insights into the evolution of the Local Group of galaxies.  The South Pole Wall is a significant extension of this interaction zone and a recent study of the SMC's movement in relation to the LMC suggests that the SMC and LMC interacted with the North Arm of the South Pole Wall.  The study further reveals that the North Arm is a result of this interaction.  The study also shows that the North Arm and the SMC interact with the Magellanic Stream, a vast, inter-galactic cloud.  The study concludes that the North Arm, SMC and the Magellanic Stream are part of a single interaction zone, known as the South Pole Wall system, and a recent study of the SMC's movement in relation to the Magellanic Clouds suggests that the SMC is moving towards the Magellanic Clouds.

Smart grid management is hindered by the prevalence of electricity theft, making it a significant concern worldwide. Deep learning techniques, particularly those involving recurrent neural networks, hold promise in detecting electricity theft due to their ability to analyze sequential data and capture complex time-related patterns. This research introduces a new approach, the deep bidirectional GRU network combined with a graph convolutional network, for identifying electricity theft. The proposed model leverages the capabilities of both techniques, using the former to analyze time-of-use data and energy consumption in specific intervals, and the latter to identify abnormal consumption patterns via graph convolutional networks. The method was tested using a dataset from 2017 provided by the Ontario Electricity Board, yielding an accuracy of 99.64% and a detection rate of 98.72%, outperforming existing research in the field.

Our research focuses on understanding how to embed tight surface graphs on the torus and Klein bottle, drawing inspiration from a concept proposed by Richard Kenyon related to embedding maps of their fundamental groups into the plane. Specifically, we have demonstrated that for a torus the most compact tight surface graphs can be represented as a product of two planar graphs, whereas for a Klein bottle they can be described as a commutative non-unital ring generated by a single element.

The lifetime of the $\Omega^0_c$ baryon has been measured for the first time using 1 and 3 inv mass samples from a 6 fb$^{-1}$ dataset of $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV $pp$ collision data collected by the LHCb detector. The measured lifetime was 150.1 $\pm$ 4.4 (stat) $\pm$ 1.1 (syst) ps, confirming the value set by the PDG. The longevity of $\Omega^0_c$ was also examined using b hadrons with $\Omega^{-}$ baryons, resulting in a lifetime measurement of 143.2 $\pm$ 10 $\pm$ 1 ps, and further supporting the value set by the PDG. The experiment's sensitivity was enhanced through the implementation of a novel event selection method.

The primary objective of unsupervised learning is to discover intrinsic data patterns and relationships without relying on labeled information. In the context of remote sensing, spectral clustering has been a prominent unsupervised learning approach, typically utilizing spectral information to identify homogeneous subgroups within images. However, existing solutions often fall short in accommodating large-scale, multi-spectral, and multi-source image analysis. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel subspace clustering method for remote sensing that leverages both spectral and spatial information. By projecting remote sensing images into lower-dimensional spaces, our approach enables the discovery of intrinsic clusters. Furthermore, a spatial regularization technique is integrated to refine the clustering results and mitigate the impact of image noise. Experimental evaluations on synthetic and real-world remote sensing datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method in outperforming traditional spectral and spatial clustering techniques.

Arctic sea ice is a critical component in the Earth's climate system, and its thermal conductivity and reflective qualities heavily depend on underlying ocean temperature and salinity. To study the implications of ocean warming and changing salinity, researchers have created synthetic ice cover samples and investigated their albedo and thermal conductivity. These samples were then compared to idealized versions used in global sea ice models. The results of laboratory and model experiments reveal consistent values for albedo and thermal conductivity. Specifically, the studies demonstrate that evaporation and melt-related processes have a negligible impact on both parameters. Furthermore, the findings suggest that ocean salinity has a minimal effect on albedo, but significantly influences thermal conductivity. Moreover, the researchers identified a correlation between salinity and temperature for both albedo and thermal conductivity. These relationships can be approximated by specific mathematical functions, which can be applied to global sea ice models.

We have successfully applied the principle of quantum Zeno suppression in an experiment, where we manipulated the interaction between cold atoms and molecules by applying a series of discrete, dynamic magnetic fields. This approach, known as a discrete Zeno scheme, allowed us to control the rate at which the atoms collided with the molecules and even selectively create final states such as the ground state molecular combination. To achieve this, we carefully optimized the frequency and intensity of the dynamic fields, taking into account the different possible outcomes of the collision process and how they interacted with the atomic and molecular system. By using a theoretical model to analyze the interaction process, we were able to identify the optimal parameters for the dynamic fields and verify that they could be used to create the desired final states. This work represents an important step towards using ultracold atom-molecule interactions to create and control specific types of molecules, and we believe it could also have practical applications in the field of quantum gas experiments.

We examine and expand on the nonextensive generalization of the Fermi-Dirac statistics, specifically for the anti-Fermi particles, also known as the Fermi-Bose anomaly at a quantum level. A similar approach can be applied to the boson world using the Bose-Einstein statistics, resulting in a generalized theory that maintains the generalization's fundamental conservation laws while maintaining consistency with the Tsallis parametrization. This theory is then applied to the generalized entropy and mass function of the anti-particulates, and it's demonstrated how the generalized entropy can be expressed as the anti-canonical form of the generalized entropy associated with the Bose-Einstein statistics, while maintaining the generalized entropy's consistency. This theory is then applied to the generalized mass function of the anti-particulates, and it's demonstrated how the generalized mass function can be expressed as the anti-canonical form of the generalized mass function associated with the Bose-Einstein statistics, while maintaining the generalized entropy's consistency.

We have discovered a new class of topological insulators, known as Floquet Weyl semimetal states, achieved by periodically driving a 3D massless Dirac semimetal with a specific driving pattern. These driven states exhibit a unique number of Floquet-Bloch states at the Weyl nodes, determined by the symmetry of the driving pulse at a particular point in the Brillouin zone. By using Floquet-Bloch theory, we identified the conditions necessary for these states to emerge, including the pattern of symmetry in the driving pulse and its relationship to the Brillouin zone. Furthermore, we found that these states can be stabilized by adjusting the strength of the driving force, allowing for a wide range of Floquet-Bloch states to be achieved. Our research has also revealed that these states can be transformed into Floquet Chern insulator states, characterized by a different number of Floquet-Bloch states at the Weyl nodes, through a process known as symmetry breaking.

This work presents Computation--Time Lock, a novel decentralized computing service that enables seamless, secure and efficient computation outsourcing without requiring a trusted intermediary. By integrating blockchain technology with smart contracts and a novel lock--out mechanism, the service incentivizes correct computations while rejecting malicious ones. Our solution offers several key benefits. Firstly, it ensures that computations are executed accurately by incentivizing honest miners with a reward for each correct solution submitted to the blockchain. Secondly, it ensures that computations are time--locked securely by encrypting data and holding the corresponding decryption key in an escrow account. Thirdly, it enables high performance through parallel processing of computations. Our design was thoroughly tested through simulations of different scenarios.

Optimizing rate-distortion efficiency in 3D point cloud video (PDV) coding poses significant challenges due to its highly complex and non-linear nature. The conventional method of rate-distortion optimization (RDO) significantly improves coding efficiency but encounters substantial computational hurdles. This paper presents a novel non-iterative RDO approach, grounded in machine learning, tailored specifically for PDV coding. It leverages a machine learning-based latent representation of distortion to bypass the need for time-consuming distortion computation associated with the traditional method. The resulting non-iterative RDO algorithm exhibits computational efficiency comparable to that of the iterative RDO method while achieving superior rate-distortion performance. The proposed RDO system has been successfully integrated into the 3D video coding standard and achieved significant rate-distortion performance enhancements, surpassing the baseline system by an average of 0.35 dB and 0.31 dB for RD-1 and RD-2 lossy coding, respectively, and providing an average improvement of 0.20 dB and 0.16 dB for lossless coding.

The QCD phase diagrams for two and three-flavor models, aligned with lattice simulations, are established. We derive the boundaries of the $\mu$-versus-$T$ phase diagrams for the chiral transition by combining the three-loop Polyakov-Nambu- Jona-Lasinovic potential and mean-field approximation. We replicate the strong coupling of confinement and the first order nature of the deconfinement transition, as observed in lattice simulations. We compare these with the phase boundaries derived from the three-loop Polyakov-Nambu- Jona-Lasinovic potential and first-order transition, coupled with a three- flavor Polyakov loop model, to determine the coincidence of the chiral and deconfinement transition lines, as suggested by recent studies.

Self-supervised learning has gained significant interest for addressing the scarcity of ground truth labels, particularly within the medical imaging domain. A prominent area of application for this method is the development of contrast-enhanced ultrasound image generation from non-contrast images. Our research introduces a new contrast ultrasound simulation method, which utilizes a single modality to optimize the training process. Our proposed Self-supervised Contrast Ultrasound Image Generation (SCUI-Gen) framework leverages three key components: a feature disentangling mechanism, a contrast-preserving loss, and a cross-entropy-based label generation system. We evaluated our framework using 1,000 training samples from a real dataset and 10,000 generated samples from a baseline model. Our results demonstrate that SCUI-Gen successfully produces high-quality contrast-enhanced images, with an accuracy of over 97% in lesion detection when integrated with SqueezeSeg2.

A significant drawback of traditional font creation is the extensive time required to compile and iterate, resulting in a high font production cost. To address this, we've developed a technique for generating few-shot fonts, which leverages a large font pre-training model and can produce high-quality typefaces with minimal examples. Our approach involves a large-scale, vector-based font model that is pre-trained on a large corpus of fonts. When generating a few-shot font, the model is fine-tuned using only a few examples of the desired typeface. While this process can be time-consuming, it significantly outperforms traditional font production methods in terms of both speed and quality. Furthermore, our technique allows for even faster results through knowledge distillation, utilizing a smaller, more efficient model that can generate high-quality fonts in real-time.

We investigate how the coupling of a charged fluid to spacetime torsion and background charge affects black hole solutions in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet theory, focusing on both thermal equilibrium and condensation phenomena. In particular, we examine torsional coupling effects in neutral and charged black holes, and find that a dimensionless parameter, $f$, which measures the strength of this interaction, significantly impacts the structure of these solutions for both equilibrium and non-equilibrium conditions. Additionally, we identify a stability anomaly associated with this interaction, which manifests as a minimum in the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of certain black holes for small $f$ values.

This paper introduces a novel approach to video streaming that utilizes digital twins for personalized experience enhancement. Given the substantial cost and energy involved in collecting samples for user quality of experience prediction, we develop a method to efficiently train a user-specific digital twin model and a shared model from these predictions, allowing for accurate prediction of video quality. To achieve this, we propose an optimization algorithm that minimizes the difference in user quality of experience predictions between the two models through an iterative and approximating solution. As a result, users can enjoy a personalized streaming experience by enabling their individualized digital twin model to adjust the video streaming process in response to changes in environment or user state, while the shared model leverages collective knowledge to jointly optimize quality of experience for all users. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in accurately predicting quality of experience and improving user quality of experience.

The detection of high-energy neutrinos by the IceCube collaboration has led to the recognition of their presence in our atmosphere for the first time. By studying these neutrinos, scientists can gain insight into how the universe operates. This research focuses on the effects of the Earth's atmosphere on neutrino oscillations, finding that the observed flavor ratio of neutrinos at Earth is approximately 1:1:6, confirming theoretical predictions. Additionally, researchers have identified a correlation between neutrino events and gamma-ray sources, which is a significant discovery that may be linked to neutrino emission from these cosmic sources.

We establish the almost certain global solvability of a periodic Schrödinger equation with a nonlinearity of the form $u \mapsto \sum_{|n \in \mathbb Z^*\} u_n^2 \hat{v}_n, \hat{n} \in \mathbb Z\setminus \mathbb Z_{\pm}[1, L^{(l)}], l \in \mathbb N$, or more generally, for any nonresonant nonlinearity in $l \in \mathbb N$. This is achieved by proving the almost certain global solvability for the Schrödinger map equation with a nonlinearity of the form $u \mapsto \sum_{|n \in \mathbb Z^*} u_n^2$, under the condition that the energy of the initial data is below the ground state energy of the linearized equation at the origin.

Human control of machines relies heavily on high-throughput feedback systems, often incorporating communication latency in the range of tens to hundreds of milliseconds. However, even with minimal latency, high feedback rates come with increased packet errors due to wireless channels and multi-access interference. To mitigate this, we developed a new Kalman-based feedback control scheme utilizing predictive control that demonstrates improved performance compared to existing solutions. Our results highlight the importance of accurate prediction in achieving reliable real-time feedback, particularly under feedback rate constraints.

A comprehensive analysis of Sgr A East, a supernova remnant associated with a high-energy source at the center of the galaxy, has been conducted. Observations of this remnant were made using the Spitzer Space Telescope and a Chandra sub-array study were compared to existing data from the Spitzer images and other sources to form a coherent image of this complex structure. The results indicate that Sgr A East can be explained by the interaction of shock waves and clouds of gas, with the longest known filament approximately 3.5 arcminutes long. Furthermore, it has been determined that Sgr A East is approximately 10,000 to 20,000 years old and is powered by the energy of the central star. The high-energy radiation of this star is also found to be interacting with the surrounding gas, producing a complex pattern of emission. The results also indicate that the high-energy radiation is responsible for the emission from the northwestern part of the bubble, as well as the emission from the molecular gas in the surrounding area. The emission from the molecular gas is found to be due to the emission from the molecular hydrogen, with the emission from the northwestern part of the bubble being due to the emission from the emission-line ions. The results also indicate that Sgr A East is composed of a mixture of emission from the central star and the surrounding gas, with the northwestern part of the bubble being a distinct feature.
